name: single-responsibility
why: A component with multiple reasons to change is fragile — a change for one reason risks breaking the other.

signals.description: component has one stated purpose
changes cluster around one concern

name: open-closed
why: A component that must be modified to extend is brittle — extension without modification is the design goal.

signals.description: new behavior added without modifying existing code
extension point exists for the kind of change being made

name: dependency-inversion
why: High-level policy depending on low-level detail inverts the dependency — the detail should conform to the policy.

signals.description: high-level module imports from low-level module
abstraction depends on detail rather than the reverse

name: interface-segregation
why: A consumer forced to depend on methods it does not use couples it to changes in those methods.

signals.description: consumer uses a subset of the interface
interface has methods irrelevant to this consumer

name: liskov-substitution
why: A subtype that surprises callers of the base type breaks the contract the base type advertised.

signals.description: subclass overrides method with different semantics
subclass strengthens preconditions or weakens postconditions

name: observer
why: One-to-many notification without the subject knowing its observers — decoupling the event source from its consumers.

signals.description: component notifies registered listeners of state changes
publish-subscribe or callback registration

name: strategy
why: Encapsulate a family of algorithms so they are interchangeable — the algorithm varies independently from the client.

signals.description: algorithm selected at runtime via injection or configuration
multiple implementations behind a common interface

name: facade
why: A unified interface to a subsystem simplifies the caller's world — the complexity is behind the door.

signals.description: single entry point wrapping multiple internal components
caller interacts with simplified interface

name: god-object
why: A component that knows or does too much — it attracts changes from every direction and resists decomposition.

signals.description: component has many unrelated responsibilities
high fan-in from diverse callers
file is disproportionately large

name: shotgun-surgery
why: A single logical change requires edits scattered across many files — the concern is dispersed, not cohesive.

signals.description: one feature change touches many files
related logic duplicated across locations

name: feature-envy
why: A method that uses another object's data more than its own — the behavior belongs with the data it reads.

signals.description: method accesses another module's internals extensively
logic belongs closer to the data it operates on

name: leaky-abstraction
why: An abstraction that forces callers to understand what is behind it — the seam is transparent when it should be opaque.

signals.description: caller handles implementation details of the abstraction
abstraction exposes internal state or error shapes

name: circular-dependency
why: Two components that depend on each other — changes in either can break the other, and neither can be understood alone.

signals.description: module A imports from module B and B imports from A
bidirectional coupling between components

name: premature-abstraction
why: An abstraction built for hypothetical future requirements — it adds complexity without current value.

signals.description: abstraction has exactly one implementation
interface designed for cases that do not exist yet
